image_description: A close-up, side-profile photograph of the head and upper neck of a Nile crocodile. The subject is facing left, with its mouth slightly open, revealing interlocking conical teeth. The skin texture is highly detailed, showing rough, bony scutes on the dorsal surface and smoother scales near the jawline. The eye is visible with a reptilian appearance. The background is a soft-focus blur of dry grass and earth.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snout tapers distinctly towards the nostrils, forming a V-shape characteristic of crocodiles rather than the U-shape of alligators. The profile matches the taxonomic description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows large, white, conical teeth. The fourth tooth on the lower jaw appears to fit into a notch in the upper jaw, confirming the 'interlocking' description even with the mouth slightly agape.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is positioned high on the skull (dorsal). While the pupil shape is hard to resolve perfectly due to lighting/resolution, the placement and general reptilian structure are correct. No obvious AI artifact in the eye region.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The nostril is clearly visible at the very end of the snout, consistent with the anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the head and neck are visible; the full body length cannot be verified from this crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The top of the head and neck show distinct, raised, bony textures consistent with osteoderms/scutes. The pattern looks natural and non-repetitive.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is a mix of muddy grey and brown, and the texture is visibly rough and granular, matching the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside of the jaw/neck is partially visible but shadowed and not clear enough to definitively verify scale shape or color as 'pale yellow/white rectangular scales'.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Limbs are completely out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the species identification (Nile Crocodile vs. other crocodilians) based on snout shape and tooth arrangement.
To analyze the micro-texture of the scales for signs of AI smearing or repetitive patterns and check edge sharpness against the background.
To ensure the teeth are structurally connected to the jawbone and not floating or fused incorrectly, a common AI failure mode.

focus_areas: Skin texture realism (scutes vs smooth scales)
Edge definition between subject and bokeh background
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the transition between the teeth and the gum line. AI often blurs this boundary. Also, verify if the eye reflection is consistent with a single light source, as inconsistent reflections can indicate composite generation.
